transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Olivia Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme Head of ML), Priya Nair (Acme Platform Eng), Ethan Brooks (Acme Security)
---
Summary (auto-generated): Discuss migration path from OpenAI + vLLM to Redwood Dedicated/Private; baseline metrics, eval parity concerns, security/compliance questions, and next steps for a benchmark POC.
---
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood. Real quick intros?
[00:08] Jordan: Jordan Lee, Head of ML at Acme. We run a mix of hosted OpenAI calls and an on-prem v LLM cluster for inference caching, um, to handle spikes.
[00:19] Priya: Priya, platform team. I own infra and deployment stuff.
[00:22] Ethan: Ethan, security. I'll be focused on compliance questions.
[00:26] Olivia: Olivia Chen, solutions engineer at Redwood — I'll focus on technical mapping and the POC.
[00:31] Samir: Cool. Goal for today is to understand your stack, what isn't working, and see if Redwood Dedicated or Private is a fit. We'll cover parity, performance, and security.
[00:40] Jordan: Great. So short version — cost and consistency. Our product calls are heavy; OpenAI is simple but costs are getting high at scale. We built a vLLM edge cluster to reduce cost for top-user cohorts but it's a maintenance burden and we see output drift vs OpenAI. We're trying to see if we can move to a single vendor that gives us predictable latency and lower unit cost but with output quality close to OpenAI.
[01:05] Olivia: When you say drift, are you seeing differences in generations for the same prompts between OpenAI and vLLM?
[01:11] Jordan: Yeah, exact same prompt, same temperature, different outputs; sometimes v LLM tokenization or sampling config — so parity is the main concern. Also embeddings subtle differences for search indexing.
[01:23] Priya: And from infra side — our vLLM cluster is on k8s with mixed A100s and 80GB cards, we handle KV caching ourselves. We want to avoid having to manage that long-term; dedicated infra with predictable throughput would be great.
[01:37] Ethan: Security: we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS for keys. If we go private/on-prem we have extra constraints about air-gapped deployments.
[01:48] Samir: Totally, all of those are typical. Quick clarifying question — which OpenAI models are you using as the truth? GPT-4? GPT-4o? And how many tokens/month roughly?
[01:58] Jordan: Mainly GPT-4, some gpt-4o for experimental features. Token volume is around 1.5B tokens/month now and growing. Latency SLOs: 300-500ms p95 for interactive features. Batch workloads can be higher latency.
[02:13] Olivia: Perfect. Couple of things we'll want to baseline: token accounting differences, tokenizer differences (bpe vs tiktoken-ish mismatches), and model mapping — which open models map closest to your current output. Redwood has curated profiles and we can run an eval harness.
[02:28] Jordan: How close do you typically get? Our main risk is user-facing regressions.
[02:33] Olivia: For many customers we hit pretty high parity with careful prompt tuning and occasionally light RLHF/temperature adjustments. We'll run an A/B parity test during the POC; we'll quantify BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics and human evals for a small sample set. v LLM and TGI are known to have sampling/runtime differences, so results vary.
[02:50] Priya: On the infra side: if we choose Dedicated, do we control instance types or is it a managed pool? We want predictable throughput and sometimes pinned latency for certain routes.
[02:59] Samir: Dedicated is a reserved GPU pool managed by Redwood but you can configure capacity tiers and autoscaling policies. For strict latency you can pin routes to higher-tier instances or dedicate capacity. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you more control — Private on-prem is a heavier lift but addresses air-gapped needs.
[03:14] Jordan: Sounds good. What about function calling and tool support? We use OpenAI function-calling for structured outputs and it's important that calls behave the same.
[03:23] Olivia: We support function/tool calling in our hosted API and the Dedicated/Private runtimes include the same SDK semantics. There are occasional differences in JSON serialization or argument ordering depending on the model runtime; we'll capture those in the parity tests.
[03:36] Ethan: Encryption: do you support customer-managed KMS in Dedicated? How about HSM?
[03:41] Samir: Yes — Dedicated supports integration with customer KMS and for Private we can do HSM integrations depending on the engagement. We'll share the security whitepaper and SOC2 cert.
[03:50] Jordan: Benchmarking — we already have a micro-benchmark against vLLM that measures p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens. Can Redwood run equivalent tests?
[03:58] Olivia: Absolutely. For the POC we'll run your prompt set across the candidate model(s) on Redwood Dedicated and measure latency, throughput, cost-per-token, kv-cache hit rates, and output deltas. If you have the scripts we can run them; otherwise we'll adapt.
[04:12] Jordan: We do have a scripts repo. We'll share a subset of prompts and an evaluation rubric.
[04:16] Samir: Great. A few potential gotchas to call out: token accounting differences can make direct cost comparisons tricky — we'll normalize to tokens consumed by the same tokenizer and show both raw token count and normalized. Also, warm KV cache behavior can affect latency; we'll surface cache hit/miss stats.
[04:33] Priya: Any limits on model file sizes or custom model artifacts for Private? Because we run some fine-tuned variants.
[04:40] Olivia: Private can accept customer-provided model weights if licensing allows; for Dedicated hosted we generally serve curated/verified open models and partner models. For private on-prem we can support custom artifacts with an onboarding process.
[04:53] Jordan: About costs — our main goal is unit cost reduction at scale. How do you price Dedicated commits vs hosted?
[04:59] Samir: Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits. Pricing is typically a combination of instance-hours commitment and token-processing units; we'll send a SKU/pricing sheet after this call.
[05:10] Ethan: From a security review perspective, we'll need to see network diagrams, data flow, retention policies, and logs. Also interested in RBAC and SSO integration with our IdP.
[05:20] Samir: Absolutely; we'll include network diagrams and the SOC2 pack. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC and RBAC at the route/model level.
[05:28] Jordan: Can Redwood match OpenAI's embedding vectors? We use embeddings for semantic search and relevance ranking; even small vector differences cause drift in results.
[05:36] Olivia: Embedding parity is tough — we can often get very close with same model families. We'll include an embedding similarity analysis in the POC; we can report cosine similarity distributions and downstream search metric impact (MRR, recall@k).
[05:48] Priya: Operational question: how do we handle upgrades and model rollouts? We need canarying and immediate rollback if regressions occur.
[05:56] Samir: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts, A/B routing, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin traffic to an older model or to a fallback hosted tier if Dedicated capacity is constrained.
[06:06] Jordan: Good. What's typical timeline for a Dedicated POC?
[06:09] Olivia: Usually 2-4 weeks to stand up a small dedicated pool and run parity tests; if Private on-prem it's longer — 4-8 weeks depending on security approvals and network setup.
[06:19] Jordan: Okay. For the POC we'll want the following validated: 1) output parity for the top 200 prompts, 2) p95 latency under 500ms for interactive flows, 3) cost per token target — 30-40% reduction vs our current blended cost.
[06:33] Samir: That sounds very reasonable. We'll scope the POC around those KPIs.
[06:36] Ethan: One more security nuance: retention — some workloads must not be logged or stored; can you configure per-route retention policies?
[06:44] Olivia: Yes. We can set per-route retention and disable logging for certain endpoints. For Dedicated we can also keep logs in your VPC.
[06:51] Priya: Network firewall rules? We want static IPs for outbound egress to our data plane if possible.
[06:57] Samir: For Dedicated we can provide stable egress IPs and VPC peering. For Private it's inside your network, so it's handled by your infra.
[07:05] Jordan: Great. Before we dive into technical specifics — any known incompatibilities with vLLM/TGI runtimes we should flag?
[07:12] Olivia: The main differences are in sampling implementations and tokenizer versions. vLLM is often faster for certain seq lengths and supports aggressive KV cache strategies; Redwood's runtime has optimized KV cache and kernel selection that aims to match or exceed vLLM's latency in many cases, but we'll want to tune model configs. TGI sometimes has different default top-k/top-p behavior. We'll log those differences in the POC report.
[07:33] Jordan: Nice. Ok let's get into a bit more detail on the benchmark plan. We'll share a prompts set of about 200 that cover short chat, long-context, and embeddings. We'll want per-prompt diffs and a human-eval sample of maybe 30 prompts.
[07:47] Olivia: Perfect. For long-context, what's your typical sequence length?
[07:50] Jordan: Up to 8k tokens in some analytics flows. Most chats are 1-2k.
[07:55] Olivia: Our runtime supports long context and has optimizations for mixed-length workloads — we'll record memory and throughput metrics.
[07:59] Priya: On logs: we need audit trails for every request with request id mapping back to our SSO identities.
[08:05] Samir: That is supported — request-level metadata and audit logs integrated into the Console, with export to your SIEM.
[08:11] Ethan: About legal: do you accept standard enterprise T&Cs or will we need amendments for data residency?
[08:17] Samir: We usually work off a standard enterprise agreement but will add SOWs for Private/on-prem as needed for residency. We'll have legal follow up if required.
[08:25] Jordan: One question on failover: if Dedicated capacity is saturated, can we automatically spill to hosted or a smaller model to preserve user experience?
[08:34] Olivia: Yes — Smart routing policies allow fallback to hosted or to cheaper model variants; you can configure priorities. We'll show examples in the Console.
[08:42] Priya: From the migration effort perspective, how invasive is it to switch client SDKs? We want minimal changes.
[08:49] Samir: Redwood SDKs are intentionally API-compatible for common flows; function calling and streaming semantics are similar. We'll provide migration guides and code snippets. Some small auth and endpoint changes required.
[08:58] Jordan: Great. Are there customers who've migrated from OpenAI+vLLM to Redwood Dedicated we can reference?
[09:03] Samir: Yes, we have a few case studies — I'll include references, anonymized metrics for cost and latency improvements.
[09:10] Jordan: Awesome. Anything else on your side?
[09:13] Olivia: Just a quick note — for the POC we'll propose two candidate model mappings: one open model family that approximates gpt-4 style outputs, and a fallback smaller model for cost-sensitive routes. We'll run both and compare.
[09:25] Jordan: Makes sense.
[09:27] Samir: Ok let's recap. Action items: Samir will send pricing and security docs; Olivia will run parity benchmark once Jordan sends the prompt set; Jordan will share the scripts and evaluation rubric; Ethan will send security questions and firewall requirements. Does that align?
[09:41] Jordan: Yes.
[09:42] Ethan: Yep.
[09:43] Priya: Yep.
[09:44] Samir: Great. We'll aim to have the pricing and docs by Friday, and kick off the benchmark next week. Anything else before we close?
[09:53] Jordan: No, that covers it. Thanks everyone.
[09:56] Samir: Thanks — speak soon.
